deep.reconstruction:
This is a draft of what became §§4–5 of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857). It treats single-valued functions on the cut surface T' that are complex functions of z, whose values jump by constants across the cross-cuts (the period moduli), and that have prescribed singularities. The aim is the classification of Abelian integrals into three kinds and the representation of every such function as a linear combination of normalized ones. Notation: T is the n-sheeted surface of genus p (2p cross-cuts); w_1..w_p are integrals of the first kind (everywhere finite).

(1) Integrals of the second kind t. Let t become infinite at a single point ε of T, with principal part β/(z−z_ε) (my reading of the elided text: β is the coefficient of the pole). Then:
- β is arbitrary.
- By the Dirichlet-principle existence and uniqueness of the previous folio, t is determined up to an additive constant by β and the real parts of its 2p period moduli.
- So if t is one such function, set t_1 = β t + α_1 w_1 + … + α_p w_p + const with complex α_i (2p real parameters). These constants can always be chosen so that β and the real parts of the 2p periods take arbitrarily given values.
- My justification: the 2p×2p real matrix formed from the real parts of the periods of i^k w_j is non-singular. This follows from the positivity of ∫|dw|², i.e. Riemann's bilinear inequality.
- Hence every such function t' is representable in this form.

(2) Integrals of the third kind Π. Next he takes functions that become logarithmically infinite at two points ε_1, ε_2, behaving like A_1 log(z−z_1) and A_2 log(z−z_2). The case of one logarithmic point is excluded because the residues must sum to zero: A_2 = −A_1. If Π_0 is one such function, every other is Π = γ Π_0 + α_1 w_1 + … + α_p w_p + const, by the same argument as in (1).

(3) Passing from the third kind to the second kind by differentiating in the parameter. Assume the points ε are neither branch points nor at infinity, so z − z_ν is a local parameter at ε_ν (z_ν = value of z at ε_ν).
- Differentiate Π with respect to z_1, keeping A_1, the real parts of the periods (or alternatively γ and the period moduli themselves), and the value at a fixed point constant.
- Since ∂/∂z_1 [A_1 log(z−z_1)] = −A_1/(z−z_1), the result is a function t that is infinite of first order at ε_1 only.
- Conversely, ∫ t dz_1 with β held constant gives back a Π.
- Likewise, repeated differentiation of t with respect to z_1 (β constant) gives functions infinite like (z−z_ν)^{−n−1} at ε (n-th derivative of 1/(z−z_1) is n!/(z−z_1)^{n+1}).
- Branch points and points at infinity are excluded here and are said to need only modifications (handled in the print with fractional local parameters).

(4) Conclusion (the decomposition theorem). Take a linear expression with constant coefficients in the w's, the Π's, the t's and their parameter-derivatives (the latter with coefficients given by the discontinuity data). It can be chosen so that it has arbitrarily given discontinuities in T' and arbitrary real parts of its period moduli. Hence every given function of the class can be so represented, which reduces every Abelian integral to the three kinds.
errors: No algebraic slips are visible. The derivative of log(z−z_1) in z_1 has the sign −1/(z−z_1), which is immaterial given the free coefficient β.

Unjustified on this page: the solvability of the linear system for the α_i, i.e. non-degeneracy of the real-part period matrix. It rests on the positivity of the Dirichlet integral, which is presumably proved elsewhere.

Subtle point: normalizing by the real parts of the periods does not make the normalized Π depend holomorphically on z_1, so the complex derivative ∂/∂z_1 is not straightforward. Riemann's parenthetical alternative (keep γ and the period moduli themselves constant, i.e. the A-normalization) avoids this. The printed 1857 text works with the holomorphic normalization.

results.what: Integrals of second kind t determined up to a constant by the pole coefficient β and the real parts of the periods; general one is β t + Σ α_i w_i + const
results.modern_name: Normalized Abelian differentials of the second kind; existence and uniqueness via Dirichlet principle

results.what: Third-kind integrals Π with logarithmic points ε_1, ε_2, A_2 = −A_1; general one is γΠ_0 + Σ α w + const
results.modern_name: Normalized Abelian integrals of the third kind (residue theorem)

results.what: Obtaining second-kind integrals and higher-order poles by differentiating Π (resp. t) with respect to the position z_1 of the singular point
results.modern_name: Differentiation of the normalized third-kind differential in the parameter (Green's-function / bidifferential approach)

results.what: Every function of the class is a linear combination of w's, Π's, t's and their parameter-derivatives
results.modern_name: Decomposition of Abelian integrals into three kinds
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1857 (anticipated in part by Abel/Legendre for elliptic and hyperelliptic integrals)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of material printed in §§4–5 of Riemann's 1857 Abelian functions paper; only the wording and the order of arguments are of archival interest.

checkable.asserts: Differentiating the logarithmic singularity in its parameter gives a simple pole (result 0).
n-fold parameter derivatives give poles of order n+1, i.e. (z−z_1)^{−n−1} (result 0).
The third-kind singularity A(log(z−z1)−log(z−z2)) has residues summing to zero, and its z1-derivative only affects ε_1, giving -1/(z−z1).

transcription_corrections: 'Ungesucht t irgend' / 'Ungesucht t' irgend' is likely a misreading of 'Ist nun t (t') irgend' or 'Bezeichnet t'...'; it introduces an arbitrary function of the class.

The function whose pole coefficient is β is t (second kind); the first line should read roughly 'Ist t in einem einzigen Punkte ε der Fläche T unendlich ... so ist für diese β willkürlich und t bis auf eine additive Constante durch die Größe β und die reellen Theile ihrer Periodicitätsmoduln bestimmt'.
'e_ν = z − z_ν' probably refers to the local parameter at ε_ν ('indem man durch z_ν den Werth von z in ε_ν bezeichnet').

The derivative step should read 'Wenn man dann Π so nach z_1 differentiirt' (differentiation with respect to the position z_1 of ε_1, not the variable z), giving 'eine Function t, die für ε_1 unendlich von der ersten Ordnung wird'.
'Umgekehrt ist ∫ t dz' should be 'Umgekehrt ist ∫ t dz_1, wenn β constant bleibt, eine Function Π'.
'wo A=0 ... β_1' likely concerns excluding a single logarithmic point (A = 0), leading to the condition A_2 = −A_1.
